source.title: Scaling Learned Image Compression Models up to 1 Billion
source.authors: Yu-Qi Li; Hao-Tian Zhang; Li Li; Dong Liu; Feng Wu

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends power-law scaling analysis to learned image compression and reports scaling results in that new setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports fitted test-loss trends for HPCM image-compression models and a same-size architecture comparison. The 2B and 10B values are forecasts, not evaluations of runs at those sizes. The rate-distortion comparisons in Table 2 are not separate tests of a power law.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of test rate-distortion loss against parameter count and Pareto-frontier training compute for learned image-compression models (HPCM, 68.5M–1B). Its own results bear on whether the power-law form holds outside language-model pretraining (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report consistent power-law scaling of test loss with model size and optimal training compute, which they say enables extrapolation to larger models. They also report that HPCM-1B achieves state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance (−24.21% BD-rate vs VTM on Kodak).
record.recipe_differences: The study fits power laws on a log-log scale using ordinary least squares, but applies them to image-compression rate-distortion loss rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy. The model-size fit uses five HPCM sizes and Kodak test loss; the compute fit uses a Pareto frontier.
record.method_sensitivity: The architecture comparison reports unstable convergence and higher test loss for Swin Transformer-based transforms than for convolution-based transforms at both tested parameter scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Swin Transformer-based transform networks at ~0.25B and ~0.5B show unstable convergence and higher Kodak test loss than same-size convolutional HPCM models (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture family (convolutional vs transformer transforms) affects loss at fixed parameter count in learned image compression.

record.problems: The scaling-law fits use only five model sizes, as the authors note. The scaling analysis is evaluated on Kodak and uses λ = 0.013. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors also state that other model designs and advanced training strategies were not explored.
record.rows_left_out: The paper forecasts L(2B) ≈ 0.7099 and L(10B) ≈ 0.6933 from the fitted model-size law, but does not evaluate models at those sizes, so these are not validation rows. Table 2 rate-distortion comparisons are not separate tests of the scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: No scaling in dataset size, no other modalities (video, generative image), no repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regimes. Only one rate point (λ=0.013) on Kodak.
Forecasts L(2B)≈0.7099 and L(10B)≈0.6933 (≈30% BD-rate vs VTM) are given but never validated against trained models.
Depth/width trade-offs at fixed parameter count are not compared. Scaled configurations mix depth and width changes without isolating shape.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked R3/R4 to V4. I unlinked them: replacing conv with Swin transforms is an architecture-family change, not the depth/width shape variation V4 names (Kaplan himself found architecture family matters, e.g. LSTM vs transformer). The V4 limits_scope label is therefore dropped. The V5 support rests on a narrow range, five points, a single-term fit without an irreducible floor, and no uncertainty. The authors list these as limitations. The extrapolations are unvalidated, so V2 is untested.

versions.untested_parts: The study scales learned image-compression models, not language models, and does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
It forecasts losses for 2B and 10B image-compression models but does not evaluate those larger runs to test prediction accuracy.
It fits loss against Pareto-frontier training compute, but does not test how the loss-minimising parameter and token allocations vary with a fixed compute budget.

The architecture comparison covers Swin Transformer-based versus convolution-based transform networks at around 0.25B and 0.5B parameters; it does not test a wide range of depth, width, or other architecture choices.
The study tests learned image compression, not other modalities or repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The study notes limited model-size granularity and uses a single-term fit, but does not compare fitting choices or demonstrate that exponents or allocation trends change with setup.

rows.subject: Five HPCM models, 68.5M to 1.0B parameters
rows.operation_detail: Fit test rate-distortion loss against model parameter count across five HPCM model sizes.

conditions.value: R + λ·D, λ = 0.013; D is mean-squared error
ordinary least squares on the log-log scale

rows.measure: Test loss as a function of model parameters
rows.note: The result is an aggregate fitted relation over five model sizes, not individually reported loss values for each model. The parameter range is 68.5M to 1.0B.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The fit spans only about 1.2 orders of magnitude (68.5M–1B) with five points. The text says the trend holds 'particularly for the three largest models'. The exponent is very small (0.0147), single-λ (0.013), Kodak only. The 1B model also drops the cross-attention context fusion module, a confound.

rows.subject: Five HPCM models, 68.5M to 1.0B parameters
rows.operation_detail: Track test loss over training compute for each model size, extract the Pareto frontier, and fit loss against optimal compute on that frontier.

conditions.value: Pareto frontier of loss and training compute

rows.measure: Test loss against optimal training compute Cmin
rows.note: This is an aggregate fit to the extracted Pareto frontier. It does not report a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. It is a single-term fit to the Pareto frontier of training curves, with no uncertainty reported. Dataset size is not varied separately.

relationships.condition: HPCM learned image-compression models, 68.5M–1B params, Kodak, λ=0.013, single-term log-log OLS fit
relationships.reason: Test RD loss follows power laws in N (α=0.0147, r=-0.98) and Pareto-frontier compute (α=0.0172, r=-0.98), over only ~1 order of magnitude with five sizes (R1, R2).
relationships.display_finding: Test rate-distortion loss has power-law exponents 0.0147 for parameters and 0.0172 for frontier compute, both with r = −0.98 across five sizes spanning about one decade.
